what: The real image of a Genesis is shown as a round portrait above its character and beside its team slot.
method: node tools/unity/qualify_webgl.mjs in headless Chrome (software WebGL), Party Menu, Create, Start, on-screen stick pushed up for 4.5 s.
observed: Preparation screen: the portrait of CHOG #1287 (red skin, TISM cap, glasses, green background) sits to the left of the first slot of team 1.
Match: the same portrait is above the label 'CHOG #1287'; the bot labelled 'CHOG #200' also carries a portrait.

Server log of that run: /genesis-art/256/1287.jpg, 200.jpg, 63.jpg and 166.jpg answered 200; 483.jpg and 459.jpg answered 404 because those copies were not made yet, and those bots simply had no portrait.

image_source.mirror_used: https://ipfs2.seadn.io/ipfs/ (bytes for 1287.webp hash to 41e70c8b..., identical to ipfs.filebase.io)
image_source.copies: .artifacts/genesis-art/256/{metadata id}.jpg, 256 px JPEG, about 20 KB each, with a provenance line per file in .artifacts/genesis-art/manifest.jsonl

tests: Five EditMode tests of Chog.Match (URL token, portrait folder) pass when run outside Unity with a reflection runner; they were not run in the Unity Test Runner.
limits: Software rendering, one client: says nothing about the phone, where the portrait is about a centimetre wide at most and its legibility is still to be judged by the user.
The image copies are local test files; the right to redistribute the art is not established.
Only the Genesis whose metadata is recorded have a copy; the download was still running at the time of this record.
No tint from Skin or Background and no change to the 3D body: the hero is still the sample's Knight, Archer or Spellcaster.
